title: Segmentation
html:
Segmentation turns unified profiles into audiences the business can act on — and it is where "data" finally becomes "marketing, sales, and service value". This phase covers the segment builder, container objects, nested segments, publish schedules, segment attributes, and the precise vocabulary of membership and qualification.

Learning Objectives

By the end of this phase, you will be able to:

  • Build a segment over unified profiles with attributes and calculated-insight criteria.
  • Use container objects and nested segments for multi-step qualification.
  • Distinguish static vs dynamic (real-time) segments and pick publish schedules.
  • Select segment attributes to ship with the audience.
  • Mirror the logic in SegmentMembershipService and Segment_Sync_Log__c.

1. What a Segment Is

A segment is a saved description of an audience: a filter over Unified Individuals (and optionally Accounts) using profile attributes, calculated-insight values, relationship/event criteria, and nested sub-segments. Every time it runs it produces segment membership — the list of individuals who currently qualify.

text
Segment "High-Value At-Risk Retail"
  criteria: Loyalty_tier IN ('Gold','Platinum')
         AND Churn_Score >= 0.7
         AND Total_Spend >= 5000
         AND Has_purchased_in_90_days = true

Membership vs qualification

  • Membership = the current set of profiles matching the criteria.
  • Qualification = the process (and event) of an individual joining or leaving the set. Real-time segments track qualification events — this powers real-time journeys and data actions ("the moment a high-value customer meets the churn rule, alert the service team").

2. Segment builder: criteria and scope

The builder has three levers:

LeverExampleNotes
TargetUnified IndividualsAlways the person-level target for audiences
Criteriaattribute =/▷/IN; insight value; events; datesFilters combine with AND/OR groups
Time window"purchased in last 90 days", "opened email in 7 days"Relative dates, not fixed literals — critical for recurring segments

Container objects

A container object lets you scope a branch of criteria to a group of related records rather than the profile itself. Example: "individuals who have an order where totalamount > 100 and a service case where status = 'Open'" — each branch runs against its container of orders/cases, and the profile qualifies only if some record in the container satisfies it. This prevents cross-record false matches and is an exam favourite.

Nested segments

Segments can reference other segments as criteria ("members of the Gold segment AND the Cart_Abandoners segment"). Nested segments reuse tested logic and avoid duplicating complex criteria. Cycles are not allowed — build a DAG, not a loop.

3. Static vs dynamic publish

Static segmentDynamic (real-time) segment
MembershipCalculated on the schedule/publishEvaluated continuously (requires streaming data)
UseBatch campaigns, daily audiencesReal-time journeys, customer 360 events, moment-based actions
ActivationRefresh on a scheduleCan trigger real-time data actions

Rule of thumb: static = plan for tomorrow; dynamic = react now. If a journey must start the moment a high-value customer abandons a cart, the data has to be streaming and the segment dynamic with a real-time activation.

4. Segment attributes

When you publish a segment you don't send raw rows — you choose segment attributes (the columns) to include for each member. Typical attributes: IndividualId, email, phone, Total_Spend, Loyalty_Tier, Churn_Score. These become the fields available in the activation target (e.g. the Marketing Cloud data extension columns). Selecting too many attributes wastes quota; selecting too few breaks downstream personalization — match attributes to the activation's use case.

Audit and refresh

  • Every segment publish writes a run record (audit/sync log) — the lab's Segment_Sync_Log__c mirrors exactly this.
  • Refresh types: on-demand, scheduled (daily/interval), or real-time for dynamic segments.
  • Monitor export status (published count vs total membership) in the activation/segment run views.

5. The Lab: SegmentMembershipService

apex
public with sharing class SegmentMembershipService {
    // For every target record: does it satisfy (profileCriteria && insightCriteria)?
    public static Map<Id, Boolean> evaluate(Set<Id> targetIds) { ... }

    // Persist one row per qualifying member (bulk upsert by external key)
    public static void syncMembers(Id segmentId, Set<Id> memberIds) { ... }
}

It demonstrates: (1) evaluate each target against the criteria set, (2) boundary guard on empty target sets, (3) a single bulk upsert keyed on the member's external key, and (4) returning counts so a caller can log the run. Its test asserts membership inclusion/exclusion at the threshold boundary and that syncMembers upserts (updates not duplicates).

Hands-On Exercises

Exercise 1: Build a segment

Write the criteria set for "VIP at-risk retail customers for a win-back email": loyalty Gold+, spend ≥ 5,000, churn score ≥ 0.6, last purchase ≥ 60 days ago. State which criteria come from the unified profile, which from a calculated insight, and the time window used.

Exercise 2: Container scoping

Build the criteria for "customers with at least one open case and one high-value order". Explain why a container object is required rather than simple profile attributes, and what can go wrong if you flatten it.

Exercise 3: Static vs dynamic decision

Scenario: SaaS portal — a churn-risk alert that must page the CSM within 5 minutes of the score dropping. Choose static or dynamic, and justify with the streaming/real-time constraint.

Exercise 4: Lab test

Add a test to SegmentMembershipServiceTest that evaluates 5 candidate profiles against threshold criteria and asserts exactly the 2 qualifying members are returned and persisted once each (no duplicate sync rows).

Key Terms Glossary

TermDefinition
SegmentA saved audience definition (filter) over unified profiles.
MembershipThe current set of individuals in a segment.
QualificationThe event/process of an individual joining (or leaving) a segment.
Container objectScopes criteria to a group of related records for part of the rule.
Nested segmentA segment referenced as criteria by another segment.
Segment attributeA profile column selected to ship with segment members on activation.
Static segmentMembership recomputed on schedule.
Dynamic/real-time segmentMembership tracked as streaming data arrives.

Certification Checkpoints

  • I can build a segment from profile attributes + insight values + time windows.
  • I can explain when a container object is required and why.
  • I can nest segments safely (DAG, no cycles).
  • I can choose static vs dynamic and the matching activation refresh.
  • I can select segment attributes deliberately.
  • I can extend and test SegmentMembershipService.

Self-Check

  1. Q: A win-back journey must start the instant a Gold customer's churn score crosses 0.7. What do you need? — A: Streaming data for the score, a dynamic segment, and a real-time activation/data action (static segments only refresh on schedule).
  2. Q: Two criteria that each look at "any order" combine wrongly on the profile. — A: Use a container object so each branch is evaluated within its own related-record set.
  3. Q: Which fields travel with segment members to Marketing Cloud? — A: Only the segment attributes you explicitly selected for the activation.
